accent.note: Also the positive/credit colour. A mint figure always means money moving toward the user.

bg.note: The page, and the on-accent text colour. The neutral ramp below is the project's own surface/text scale, not synthesised.

bgCard.note: First tonal step. Cards, dialogs, tab bar, inputs.

bgCardElevated.note: Second tonal step. Controls sitting on a card: chips at rest, dialog secondary buttons, avatar wells.

bgInput.note: Same value as bgCard, kept separate to express intent.

border.note: The workhorse 1px rule: card borders, dividers, separators, progress-bar tracks, tab bar top edge.

borderLight.note: Lifted rule for dialog edges and secondary-button outlines.

textPrimary.note: Off-white with a green cast. Amounts, names, titles, input values.

textSecondary.note: Labels, supporting copy, metadata. 6.8:1 on bgCardElevated, the lightest surface and therefore the binding one.

textMuted.note: 4.5:1 on bgCardElevated — exactly on the AA floor. Hints, timestamps and inactive states only, never text a user must read to finish a task.

positive.note: Identical to accent by design. Income, credit, owed-to-you, healthy budget.

negative.note: Money owed, expenses, destructive actions, form errors, over-budget.

warning.note: The single middle state: budget between 70% and 90% of limit. Appears nowhere else.

accent10.note: The wash step of the Tinted Wash Rule. Active chips, icon wells.

accent20.note: The border step of the Tinted Wash Rule.

white05.note: Micro badges inside list rows, e.g. the SETTLED pip.

display.purpose: The one figure a screen is about — the dashboard net balance. Never more than one per screen.

headline.purpose: The hero figure of a secondary card, e.g. budget spend-to-date.

figure.purpose: Supporting amounts inside a card — balance halves, per-member totals.

figureSmall.purpose: Stat-card amounts in a multi-up row.

title.purpose: The user's own name in the dashboard header. The only body-face type this large.

heading.purpose: Stack-screen page titles beside the back control.

subheading.purpose: Section titles, card titles, empty-state headlines.

body.purpose: Row labels, dialog messages, content copy.

caption.purpose: Supporting copy, hints, toast text, secondary links.

label.purpose: Card eyebrows, legend text, metadata. Often uppercase.

overline.purpose: Input field labels. The widest tracking in the system.

micro.purpose: Status pips inside rows, e.g. a SETTLED badge.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: The toast. The only true overlay element in the app.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: A floating action button over a scrolling list.

shadows.name: lifted-accent
shadows.native: shadowColor PC.accent, shadowOffset {0,3}, shadowOpacity 0.4, shadowRadius 8, elevation 6
shadows.purpose: The group-detail FAB only — an accent-tinted variant of lifted.

motion.name: press-ripple
motion.purpose: Material ripple from the point of contact, via components/Touchable.jsx. Neutral by default; tone="accent" uses rgba(6,10,9,0.18) on a solid mint fill; borderless for anything with a shadow. activeOpacity is no longer used anywhere in the app.

motion.name: micro
motion.purpose: Appear/dismiss of small elements — toast entry, sheet backdrop.

motion.name: transition
motion.purpose: Sheet and overlay movement, value changes a user should notice.

motion.name: ambient
motion.purpose: Progress-bar and ring fills, skeleton shimmer — motion that reports rather than responds.

motion.name: engine
motion.purpose: All animation uses core Animated with default easing. react-native-reanimated is installed but not used for app motion; no custom Easing curves are defined anywhere.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: The sole target. Edge-to-edge with safe-area insets applied per screen. No tablet or landscape layout exists.

narrative.overview:
PayCircle reads like a trading desk that happens to live in a student's pocket. The ground is near-black with a faint teal warmth, the structure is drawn in hairlines rather than boxes, and the numbers — the only thing anyone actually opens the app for — are set in monospace so they can be read exactly rather than approximately. A single electric mint is the one voice that rises above the dark, and it speaks only about money and action.

The system is precise, engineered and calm. Precise, because every figure is a claim about what someone owes and the typography treats it that way. Engineered, because depth comes from tonal layers and 1px rules instead of soft shadows — the construction is visible, not hidden under blur. Calm, because the palette is almost entirely neutral: three near-black surfaces, three greys of text, and one accent that is deliberately scarce. Nothing glows for decoration.

Density is high and deliberate. Type runs small (11–15px for nearly everything that isn't a figure), cards sit 12px apart, and the page keeps a constant 20px gutter so content columns never shift between screens. The effect should be an instrument panel a student trusts at a glance, not an app that performs friendliness at them.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black teal-warm ground (#060A09) with two tonal surface steps above it
Monospace, negatively-tracked figures for every amount you stop and read
One accent (#00E5BE) that doubles as the positive/credit colour — scarcity is the point
Hairline borders (1px) and tonal steps instead of shadows
Status colour as a translucent wash, never a saturated fill
Small type, tight rhythm, constant 20px gutter

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Mint is not a brand wash, it is a signal. One mint-filled control per screen, and mint text only where it means money-toward-you, an active state, or a link. If two mint fills compete on one screen, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Tinted Wash Rule
rules.body: A status colour never fills a surface at full strength. It appears as a ~8–10% wash, a ~22–35% border of the same hue, and full-strength text or icon on top. The inline error (rgba(255,80,85,0.08) fill, rgba(255,80,85,0.22) border, negative text) is the canonical form. Saturated red or amber behind a sentence of copy is a violation.

rules.name: The Dark-On-Mint Rule
rules.body: Text and icons on a mint fill are always the ground colour, never white. Mint is bright enough that white-on-mint fails contrast and reads as a glow.

rules.name: The Stop-And-Read Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for figures a user stops and reads: the display figure, card hero figures, supporting card amounts, and stat amounts. List-row amounts stay in the body face so a long list doesn't become a wall of monospace — but they carry fontVariant: ['tabular-nums'] so the column still aligns. A row amount in full monospace, or a card hero figure that isn't, are both wrong.

rules.name: The Negative Tracking Rule
rules.body: Figures 26px and above take negative letter-spacing (−1px at 26px, −1.5px at 32px). Monospace at display size is too airy otherwise and stops reading as one object.

rules.name: The Twenty Rule
rules.body: The page gutter is 20px on every screen and is not negotiated per-screen. A card that wants to bleed wider changes its own padding, never the page's.

rules.name: The Leaves-The-Stack Rule
rules.body: A shadow is permitted only for an element that genuinely floats free of the layer stack — a toast, a FAB, a true overlay. Cards, rows, inputs, chips, sheets and headers are flat, always, and earn their separation from tone and a hairline. If something wants a shadow to feel distinct, the fix is a tonal step or a border.

rules.name: The Third Rule
rules.body: A square icon tile's corner radius is about one third of its side: 30px→10, 34px→10, 38px→12, 44px→14, 58px→18. Avatars are the exception and go fully circular. Pick the radius from the size, don't invent one.

rules.name: The Dashed-Empty Rule
rules.body: An empty container keeps its exact card geometry and switches its border to dashed. Never substitute a different fill, a lower opacity, or an illustration.

dos: Do take every colour from the PC object in constants/theme.js. It is the normative source; DESIGN.md describes it rather than replacing it.
Do hold the 20px page gutter on every screen, and change a card's own padding when something needs to sit wider.
Do set figures a user stops and reads in monospace at 700/600 with negative tracking at 26px and above, and give list-row amounts fontVariant: ['tabular-nums'] instead.
Do build depth from the bg → bgCard → bgCardElevated steps plus a 1px border.
Do express every status surface as the tinted wash: ~10% fill, ~25% border, full-strength text.
Do put dark ground-coloured text on a mint fill.
Do keep an empty state on the same card geometry with a dashed border.
Do size an icon tile's radius at roughly a third of its side.

Do give every interactive control a 48dp minimum touch target, per the accessibility standard recorded in PRODUCT.md. Expand the hit area, not the visual box: pass the rendered size to touchSlop() from constants/theme.js — touchSlop(38) for a square control, touchSlop(0, 30) for a wide short one like a chip, so only its vertical reach grows.

Do give every icon-only control an accessibilityRole and an accessibilityLabel that names the action rather than the glyph — "Scan a UPI QR code", not "scan". Toggles also carry accessibilityState (selected for chips and filters, and a label that flips, as the password reveal does between "Show password" and "Hide password").
Do guard display figures against large amounts with numberOfLines={1}, adjustsFontSizeToFit and a minimumFontScale floor. A lakh-plus balance must shrink inside its card, never overflow it.
Do cap user-supplied names with numberOfLines={1} wherever the parent is flex: 1, so a long name truncates instead of pushing the amount off the row.
donts: Don't hardcode #060A09 as the on-accent text colour. It appears literally in several files; it is PC.bg and should be referenced as such.
Don't add a shadow to a card, row, sheet, input or header. Shadows belong only to elements that leave the layer stack.
Don't fill a surface with saturated negative or warning — especially behind copy.
Don't introduce a second accent. Mint is the only voice, and it also means positive money; a second hue would break that reading.

Don't use textMuted for body copy or any text a user must read to finish a task. It sits on the AA floor by design and is reserved for hints, timestamps and inactive states; content belongs in textSecondary or textPrimary.

Don't darken any text token below 4.5:1 against bgCardElevated (#131A17), the lightest surface in the system and therefore the one that sets the floor. Every token is currently measured against it, so a "slightly dimmer" variant is a regression, not a nuance.

Don't apply FONTS.* to isolated styles. Mixing a named Roboto family with the numeric fontWeight used everywhere else produces inconsistent weight rendering on Android — either convert a whole surface or leave the platform face alone.
Don't use white text on mint, and don't put mint text on bgCardElevated at small sizes without checking it.
Don't change a chip's or control's dimensions on state change. Only fill, border and text colour move, so nothing reflows.
